items.reason: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182-184 leaves negative offsets unchanged for previous cursors and passes them into Django queryset slicing, which rejects them. Cursor parsing accepts negative integers at src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:58-59, and src/sentry/api/base.py:540 catches only BadPaginationError around pagination. Although this failure existed previously, the PR directly changes the implicated slicing code; the claim about every paginated endpoint is overly broad.

The added comment at src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:26-27 claims efficient reverse pagination, but line 28 merely stores an integer, and src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182-184 passes negative reverse offsets into unsupported queryset slicing. Accepting negative integers is real; the advertised pagination capability is inaccurate documentation with no behavioral effect from the comment itself.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 guarantees start_offset equals offset whenever cursor.is_prev is true. The trimming check at lines 186-192 only executes for previous cursors, so the claimed mismatch cannot occur in that branch.
